title: Sensor hardening and evidence quality
summary: Signed sensor formats and bounded GPS, camera and audio checkpoints are retained alongside proposed Goals for reliable acquisition, durable failed attempts, calibrated usability, acoustic reliability, front/back camera capture and motion, device attribution, screenshot retrieval/hardening, location/timing assurance and resistance to substitution. Independent physical acceptance remains unresolved.

goals.title: Signed evidence formats
goals.description: Implemented camera, microphone and location formats and shared appraisal. Integrity, policy satisfaction, requester receipts and committed acceptance are separate judgments; signatures do not establish physical sensor truth.

milestones.title: Signed camera, microphone and location formats
milestones.description: Challenge-bound C2PA JPEGs and WAVs and request-bound COSE location traces have shared Rust/WASM verification. Appraisal reruns the artifact verifier against independently supplied original authority and signer pins. Media pins identify certificates; location pins identify canonical SPKI. Native acquisition assertions remain application claims, and basic verification supplies neither hardware enrollment nor independent position assurance. The original achievement date is unknown.
acceptance: The implemented verifiers check complete sensor artifacts against their original request and independently supplied expected signer; audio also checks the retained transcript.
Appraisal distinguishes integrity and requested policy from physical authenticity, trusted clocks and committed acceptance; it writes no acceptance state.

goals.title: Recorded phone results and saved-file verification

milestones.title: Verify one raw-GPS proof after the phone restart
milestones.description: On 4 October the unchanged installed collector recovered raw callbacks after the owner restarted the stationary phone. One fresh proof passed independent Rust/WASM checking against the original saved before collection and the previously trusted location key. Its signed session lasted 5,713 ms, with three fixes spanning 2,001 ms and four raw epochs. This establishes that attempt's proof verification; receiver cause, recurrence, preparation speedup, physical position and permanent recovery remain unproven. No independent requester receipt or workflow acceptance was recorded.
acceptance: The retained proof passes its exact original request, trusted key, signature and requested location/raw-GNSS policy checks in Rust/WASM.
Tampered bytes, wrong request/key and substitution into the failed-attempt verifier are refused.

evidence.label: Single successful post-restart proof and limits

milestones.title: Phone GPS failure verification and exact restart retention
milestones.description: Saved phone timeout and policy-rejection reports passed separate verification. The 5 October recheck used actual native policy rejection and a simulated final-write fault: a verified signed report remained in memory, while its earlier unsigned pending journal snapshot recovered exactly after a controlled process restart, including floating-point values. Prior records retained their bytes and the initial-write-failed memory-only outcome stayed absent. The original one-ULP failed comparison remains preserved. Natural startup-status-0 report production, crashes during collection/signing/writing, power loss and genuine signing/full-storage outages remain unverified.
acceptance: Phone failure reports verify against independently retained originals and trusted keys; altered inputs and successful-proof substitution are refused, with successful-measurement and acceptance flags false.
The controlled restart recovers the new unsigned pending snapshot exactly against its pre-restart signed snapshot and preserves existing retained bytes without inventing a signed outcome.

Interrupted helper transitions remain recorded separately.

goals.title: Reliable acquisition across devices and interruptions
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: make camera, microphone and GPS acquisition, cancellation and fresh retry dependable within explicit supported device/profile limits. Investigate recorded GNSS startup failure and recurrence, distinguish preparation from qualifying observations, and characterize acquisition, signing and complete-file arrival separately before proposing performance changes. Physical cases include permission/provider changes, foreground loss, contention, route/privacy changes, longer supported recordings and process interruption; discarded AAudio stop/close results remain an observability gap. Hero 1 owns collector behavior, provenance and physical assurance; Hero 10 owns app-wide permissions/lifecycle integration and invokes cleanup; Hero 8 owns operation, cancellation and status semantics. Collectors must distinguish confirmed shutdown, failed cleanup with retained ownership and unknown release. A cancellation acknowledgment or expired lease alone cannot confirm that an unreachable device stopped. Collector entry points need Hero 2 authority/work-privacy policy through the shared Hero 8/10 grant interface, binding principal, device, operation, authoritative work-state revision, purpose, sensors, recipients, explicit consent and validity. An authentication-camera exception is limited to its initiating device/operation and current revision; authentication, reconnect or status lookup must not resume work or activate sensors. Actual authority provenance, offline limits, conflicts, sign-out invalidation, interface schema, supported devices and shared physical criteria remain unresolved. Domain responsibilities are adopted; implementation scope, task ownership and order are not.

goals.title: Inspectable outcomes and durable failed-attempt retention
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: extend the bounded GPS precedent into inspectable sensor outcomes, preserving failed attempts when later retries succeed. Hero 1 owns collector failure formats, original request/profile and enrollment context, frozen observed timing, partial observations, signing domains and explicit signed, unsigned or absent-report states. It supplies complete versus partial/failed acquisition, unavailable/unassessable quality, per-component camera/GPS outcomes, refusal reasons and observed cleanup state. Hero 8 owns the operation/status/cancel/recovery interface consuming those facts; Hero 10 implements app-wide lifecycle and bounded on-device retention/export; Hero 11 implements selected authorized hosted retention/exchange under workflow transaction semantics. Exact schemas, covered failure classes, storage capacity, export/deletion authority and crash/power-loss guarantees remain undecided. No caller status, local journal or service record may fabricate a signed outcome, renew a challenge, prove global completeness or turn cancellation acknowledgment into observed shutdown. Case handoffs preserve exact original bytes/context, profile/metric versions, uncertainty and which timing/provenance claims were independently checked. Heroes 3, 5 and 7 define participant, dispute and incident uses, preservation/disclosure requirements and any authorized interpretation or consequences. A valid failure report alone proves neither physical effort, cause, fault nor payment entitlement. The existing broader-coverage proposal remains below; its detailed format/platform steps are not yet scoped.

milestones.title: Extend inspectable failures beyond the covered GPS triggers
milestones.description: The owner prioritized inspectable failed attempts on 30 September, with separate camera/GPS component outcomes and honest signing/storage absence. Current signed GPS reports cover raw-policy rejection, the existing zero-callback timeout and startup status 0 only; permission denial, cancellation, provider loss and other uncovered failures have no signed attempt artifact. Audio diagnostics remain bounded and unsigned, with no signed camera/audio failure format or durable audio attempt journal. The wider coverage and format breakdown remain to be defined; earlier unsigned observations must remain unsigned.

goals.title: Calibrated quality requirements for usable evidence
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: turn reproducible sensor guidance into task-relevant requirements only where calibration supports them. Preserve the requested single 0–100 sharpness value with one internally managed algorithm; algorithm selection, readable-text/digit evaluation and any threshold remain open. Consider subject detail, resolution, exposure, noise/compression and explicitly unassessable outcomes rather than treating one sharpness score as usability. Define how any selected metric version, region and requirement would bind to the original signed request while retained evidence keeps its original rules. Audio usability and location uncertainty require their own semantics, including the different Android/browser confidence meanings. Assignments supplies task expectations; the dispute/governance domains decide responsibility, compensation and consequences. No quality-based rejection, penalty rule or production acceptance standard is adopted by this roadmap. The proposed participant interface distinguishes unavailable or unassessable quality from partial/failed acquisition and complete evidence, retaining the exact request/policy and reason for refusal; calibrated requirements must be fixed before collection. Other retained hardening concerns include camera exposure/detail and motion guidance, audio continuity, clipping and level observations, and location uncertainty/freshness. Quiet audio or adverse environmental conditions may be the intended observation; challenge recovery, a high sharpness value or a reported accuracy radius alone cannot establish task usability or fault.

milestones.title: Define the requested single 0–100 sharpness value
milestones.description: On 5 October the owner requested one user-facing sharpness value, an optional minimum on a 0–100 scale, and one underlying algorithm managed internally. Algorithm selection and implementation remain deferred. The notes call for reading-fidelity evaluation of representative text/digits and adverse images before enforcement; a blur score is not a percentage of readable characters. No algorithm, cutoff or signed quality contract has been agreed or implemented.

evidence.label: Recorded owner request and deferred implementation

goals.title: Reliable acoustic challenges and honest refusal
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: establish repeatable challenge recovery and defensible refusal for the supported microphone/speaker path, using the deferred offline characterization before separately scoped physical work. Examine noise, attenuated signals, repeated/late markers and detector selection, with explicit compatibility decisions before changing successful signed-WAV rules. The pilot-only fallback remains distinct from evidence detection. Characterize supported recording durations, actual routes, callback continuity and failure-diagnostic export/retention across selected devices; headphones or Bluetooth would need a separately defined profile rather than an implicit fallback. Supported acoustic conditions, error-rate targets and any detector revision remain unresolved. Challenge recovery alone proves neither sound propagation through air nor useful capture of an unrelated environmental sound. Independent physical requester acceptance remains under the requester-validation Goal.

milestones.title: Characterize challenge detection and refusal in noisy audio
milestones.description: The recorded follow-up is deferred: examine offline noise and repeated-marker fixtures before deciding whether changes or a separately authorized physical check are needed. No controlled noisy-environment result, calibrated noise limit or success rate is established. The pilot-only qualifying-peak fallback does not change signed-WAV detection; generic multiple-peak selection and stronger late-repeat ambiguity remain unresolved. Challenge detectability does not establish usability of unrelated environmental sound.

goals.title: Front/back photo capture and motion evidence
goals.description: The owner selected explicit rear-then-front sequential capture after this phone advertised no concurrent combination. Implemented signed mode/order binding, exact comparable-clock exposure gap reporting, native release-gated camera handoff, semantic UI controls and bounded public export support; strict concurrent and explicit browser single-camera modes remain distinct. The inspected developer APK is installed with exact-hash readback. Software checks passed, but the first physical sequential attempt timed out after rear bytes arrived with front pending and no signatures. A fresh retry was refused because previous cleanup remained pending. The exact resource/callback cause is unknown. Work stopped at the owner request to continue later; no verified phone pair or measured phone gap exists. Screenshot evidence collection, durable partial retention, the wider device failure matrix, real computer validation and independent requester acceptance remain unfinished.

milestones.title: Define required camera sets and capture timing
milestones.description: Implemented the bounded version-1 Rust camera-set profile and preparation/outcome contract. Explicit single-camera, concurrent front/back and owner-selected sequential front/back timing are distinct. Sequential camera-list order is required, comparable exposure starts must strictly increase, and exact nanosecond span is reported without a simultaneity or default maximum-gap claim. Missing or changed clocks remain unassessable; missing members are never dropped. Fourteen focused profile tests pass, with nine additional signed-evidence tests in the 23-test camera-set suite. Capability advertisements do not grant collection authority or prove physical behavior.
acceptance: The authored profile defines explicit single-camera/front-back membership, distinct sequential/concurrent timing, consent/authority handoffs and complete, partial, failed, unsupported and unassessable outcomes.

Fourteen focused profile tests pass for identity, role, exact order/gap, no silent reduction, unavailable concurrency, strict/bounded JSON and exact timing. Sequential mode cannot be read as permission to substitute for a concurrent request.

goals.title: Bounded location and timing assurance
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: evaluate the implemented raw-GNSS and optional independent-position profiles against real device capabilities and explicitly retained external inputs. Define acceptable uncertainty/coverage for selected tasks, distinguish receiver preparation and session duration from observation span, and measure cross-sensor timebase/freshness limits without treating device or requester clocks as independently trusted. Independent position recomputation needs maintained, independently obtained navigation inputs and a reviewed provider/trust policy; numerical consistency still does not authenticate satellite RF or physical location. Supported receiver profiles, navigation-source operations and any stronger time or capture-time assurance approach remain unresolved. Identity supplies enrollment policy, and infrastructure/server Heroes would supply any chosen trust-data distribution or durable receipt service. No new provider, capture-time attestation service or physical-position assurance level is selected here. The proposed Services boundary leaves admissible navigation sources, freshness/provenance and verification requirements with Sensors; Hero 11 may retain and distribute independently provisioned inputs if separately selected under workflow access semantics. The actual source/trust policy remains undefined, and service delivery cannot make an input independently trusted or authorize automatic acquisition.

goals.title: Resistance to replay, substitution and false sensor claims
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: define and evaluate the adversarial cases that the sensor evidence path should detect or explicitly leave outside assurance. Candidate cases grounded in current limits include old-media signing, screen or staged-scene capture, live external audio replay/digital mixing, forged native metadata and fabricated or spoofed GNSS observations. Retain exact-request, signer, transcript, complete-artifact and composition binding, and separate refusal tests from demonstrated physical resistance. Choose attacker capabilities and meaningful success criteria before making a stronger authenticity claim; neither C2PA nor key-generation attestation authenticates a later sensor stack. Identity owns enrolled-key, principal and device policy plus Operator-face liveness and trusted-capture requirements. Sensors retains generic camera/audio/GNSS acquisition provenance, substitution evaluation and capture-time evidence requirements; APK buildout implements any selected native interfaces. Infrastructure/server Heroes own durable cross-device replay/acceptance records. The sensor Goal supplies evidence semantics and scoped attack evaluation, with no assumed global replay service or production security certification.

goals.title: Device attribution and measurement continuity
goals.description: Proposed future Goal from the retained sensor-quality notes: evaluate which device-related observations can support continuity between an enrolled device, the expected Operator and its photo, audio, location or future screen-capture records. Candidate observations include an enrolled device-key identifier and, only where available and appropriate, the proposed device/MAC-derived hash; no identifier or MAC collection method is selected. Assess availability, stability, spoofing, cross-device use and privacy before binding selected observations to the original request, artifact and independently verified enrollment context. An identifier or hash alone establishes neither the human operating the device nor authenticity or anonymity. Hero 1 owns capture provenance and evidence semantics; Hero 2 owns principal/device enrollment, key authority and privacy policy; Hero 10 supplies any selected Android observations, while desktop integration and Heroes 8/11 exchange/retention remain separately scoped. This Goal records an omitted future concern, without selecting a tracking identifier, attribution guarantee or implementation plan.

goals.title: Screenshot retrieval and capture hardening
goals.description: Proposed future Goal explicitly requested by the owner: add device-screen screenshot acquisition and retrieval as a distinct evidence capability, alongside camera, microphone and location. Define supported phone/desktop capture sources and whether a request concerns a display, window, application or region; no platform adapter or capture mode is selected yet. The design should preserve deliberate source/recipient consent and work-state authority, bind selected provenance and exact captured bytes to the original request and expected signer, and expose observed capture timing, dimensions, source availability and any unverified claims. Evaluate replay, imported/edited-image substitution, stale or wrong-surface capture and ambiguous screen/display identity without equating a signature with trusted OS capture or truth of the displayed content. Define explicit refusal, cancellation, permission-revocation, protected/unavailable-content and cleanup outcomes, with bounded retention and exact-byte export/retrieval. A screenshot must remain distinguishable from a camera photograph, and development/debug screenshots do not establish a hardened screen-evidence collector. Hero 1 owns the evidence format, capture provenance, quality and substitution evaluation; Hero 2 supplies privacy/authority policy, Hero 3 task consent and review, Hero 10 any Android platform integration, Hero 8 operation/status/cancellation interfaces and Hero 11 selected authorized exchange/retention. Desktop integration, request/format/signing policy, disclosure scope, assurance limits and software versus real-device acceptance remain unresolved. The new capability is proposed; no screenshot collection or implementation has begun. The proposed Milestones below separate source/consent decisions, artifact verification, acquisition, exact retrieval, failure/cleanup behavior, software checks, actual-platform results and independent requester acceptance.

milestones.title: Define screenshot sources, consent and authority
milestones.description: Proposed specification for the requested screenshot capability: select initial phone/desktop platforms and define whether a request names a display, window, application or region. Hero 1 leads capture semantics; Heroes 2/3 supply authority, privacy and participant consent, Hero 10 Android integration and Hero 8 grant/status semantics. Desktop integration remains to be chosen. Define what source identity can actually be observed and the behavior for protected, unavailable or changed surfaces without silently widening the capture area.
acceptance: Prospective: an authored profile identifies initial supported platforms, source/region semantics, explicit recipients and deliberate consent, with authority/work-state, cancellation and permission-revocation requirements.

Prospective: the profile defines source changes, protected/unavailable content, unsupported capabilities and unavailable metadata explicitly; it chooses no capture API or assurance claim merely by recording this proposal.

milestones.title: Implement a distinct verifiable screenshot artifact
milestones.description: Proposed Rust format and verifier: select a versioned screen-evidence request/assertion and signing policy, then bind exact screenshot bytes, original request, expected signer, selected source/region and observed dimensions/timing/provenance. Preserve unknown fields as unavailable where the chosen schema permits them. Screenshots must not masquerade as camera-acquired photographs, and artifact integrity must remain separate from honest OS capture, freshness of displayed information or truth of the content.
acceptance: Prospective: actual verification checks the selected screen-artifact type, exact request/key/bytes and required provenance fields; edits, wrong context and substitution into camera evidence are refused.

Prospective: assurance output distinguishes verified integrity from unproven capture origin, clock trust and displayed-content truth, while historical camera/audio/location verification remains unchanged.

milestones.title: Acquire screenshots through a bounded selected adapter
milestones.description: Proposed collector implementation for the platform/source profile selected above. Capture only the deliberately authorized source/region and preserve available acquisition observations through the signing gate. Hero 10 owns any Android permission and app-wide lifecycle integration; desktop platform integration needs a scoped implementation decision. Hero 1 owns collector/provenance behavior. An imported image, debugging screenshot or cached prior frame must not silently become fresh screen evidence.
acceptance: Prospective: the selected adapter returns exact screenshot bytes and supported provenance for the requested source within the original authority/window, without an arbitrary-file path into fresh native capture signing.

Prospective: source changes, unavailable capture, invalid bounds and lost or insufficient consent fail explicitly without widening scope or substituting earlier pixels; any capture API limitations remain visible.

milestones.title: Export, retrieve and reverify exact screenshot bytes
milestones.description: Proposed bounded export/retrieval integration: retain the exact screen artifact with its original request, profile, verification context and available outcome records. Hero 10 implements selected Android-local storage/export; Hero 8 supplies retrieval/status interfaces and Hero 11 only separately selected hosted access/retention. Storage limits, recipients and deletion/export authority must be settled before implementation. Retrieval is a read of retained evidence and must not trigger another capture or renew freshness.
acceptance: Prospective: independently retrieved bytes, lengths and hashes equal the original retained artifact, and fresh verifier execution uses the retained original request/context plus independently supplied expected signer.

Prospective: repeated retrieval preserves originals and explicit missing/unsigned/storage-failed states, performs no new capture/signing and records no acceptance merely because a save or transfer succeeded.

milestones.title: Preserve screen-capture refusals and cleanup outcomes
milestones.description: Proposed integration with shared failure semantics for denial, protected/unavailable surfaces, source loss, revocation, expiry, cancellation and signing/storage failures. Hero 1 supplies actual collector outcomes and provenance limits; Hero 10 supplies native/app lifecycle cleanup, Hero 8 exposes status and Hero 11 retains only selected records. Respect the scoped work-state revision and prevent late permission/capture callbacks or reconnect from resuming collection. A signed screenshot failure format remains a design decision rather than an assumed capability.
acceptance: Prospective: selected negative paths expose separate acquisition, artifact/report availability and storage outcomes, including honest unsigned/absent records, without replacing a prior successful or failed attempt.

Prospective: cleanup reports confirmed release, retained ownership after failure or unknown release; cancellation acknowledgment is not used as proof of shutdown, and stale callbacks cannot sign or publish revoked work.

milestones.title: Test screenshot substitution, scope and lifecycle in software
milestones.description: Proposed software-only checkpoint with synthetic screen images, actual selected artifact verification and focused adapter/lifecycle harnesses in the managed container. Exercise rejected import paths, edited bytes, stale request/timing, changed key/source context, wrong region, protected/unavailable outcomes, bounds and cancellation/revocation races; do not claim that verification detects every fabricated image on a compromised platform. Hero 8 contributes workflow conformance and Hero 10 selected native harnesses. These checks do not demonstrate real OS capture or resistance to a compromised platform.
acceptance: Prospective: authentic retained results cover valid fixtures and altered bytes, wrong request/key, misleading camera type, wrong source/region, truncation and bounded-input refusals without substituting verifier verdicts.

Prospective: focused permission/source-change/cancellation and retrieval checks retain both failures and passing corrections, verify exact-byte preservation and show no stale publication or automatic recapture.

milestones.title: Validate actual screenshot capture and retrieval
milestones.description: Proposed platform checkpoint after supported platforms, source modes and a bounded run are selected and separately authorized. Hero 1 records actual screen-capture provenance and file verification; Hero 10 supplies Android integration observations, and the selected desktop integration supplies its own results. Check known displayed content, source identity, consent boundaries, byte-preserving retrieval and selected denial/revocation behavior. A platform capture result is separate from synthetic checks, independent requester acceptance and truth of displayed content.
acceptance: Prospective: every platform/source profile included in the selected scope has retained actual capture, original request/context, exact retrieved artifact and independent verifier results, with unavailable metadata and unsupported modes stated.

Prospective: the selected consent, source-change/refusal and cleanup cases are observed on the real platform; no ordinary debug screenshot or software simulation is counted as that platform acceptance.

milestones.title: Independently receive and accept screenshot evidence
milestones.description: Proposed independent requester/operator checkpoint for the selected real platform workflow. Hero 1 leads capture/evidence assurance; Hero 8 supplies exact request, complete-arrival receipt, verification and declared-ledger acceptance semantics; Hero 10 contributes Android behavior and Hero 11 only any selected hosted exchange. Requester identity, device/route choice, signer authority and ledger scope remain decisions. This is a screen-evidence workflow result, with no claim that it verifies the truth of another application or completes all sensor acceptance.
acceptance: Prospective: an independent requester retains original authority/source requirements and trusted pins before acquisition, receives the exact artifact and receipt/context, reverifies it and explicitly accepts once in the declared scope.

Prospective: altered/swapped bytes, stale request/timing or mismatched source claims are refused under the selected profile, retained evidence can be inspected without recapture, and local replay behavior, fresh acceptance, trusted capture and displayed-content truth remain separate claims.
